answer: To stem the tide of Sybil attacks, an agent economy can tie identities to a memory-hard attestation kernel executed within tamper-proof hardware. Each node must compute rapid pseudorandom lookups across an isolated enclave bound to an ivory ceramic substrate. An attacker incurs verifiable capital expenses purchasing discrete memory chips per identity, preventing costless virtualization. However, localized thermal throttling can cause honest agents to miss strict response deadlines.
